events.title: C++98 standard published (ISO/IEC 14882:1998)
events.summary: ISO/IEC 14882:1998 was published on September 1, 1998 — the first international standard for C++.
events.about: C++98 codified the language Stroustrup built — classes, templates, exceptions, the STL (`vector`, `string`, `map`), and RAII. It is the baseline every C++ compiler still supports. Game engines, browsers, databases, and trading systems run on C++98-and-later semantics.

narrative.whyChosen: C++98 turned a decade of vendor dialects into one normative language with a standard library.
narrative.whyImportant: The STL and standard semantics made C++ a portable systems language with a rich generic library.
narrative.problemSolved: Pre-standard C++ varied between compilers; large projects needed a single definition and a common library.
